events.text: Your island is not where you left it. It has drifted three days east in the night and parked itself beside a much grander isle. The neighbours have a pavilion, a cloud orchard and a look on their faces.

choices.text: Push it back home with qi

effects.log: It takes a week. The island resists like a mule. You arrive home sore and very strong in the shoulders. (-5 health)

choices.text: Stay and be a good neighbour

effects.log: They bring cloud plums. You bring your best tea. In a year they ask you to water the orchard while they are away.

choices.text: Tie it down with a rope of starlight

effects.log: The knot holds. You are prouder of the knot than of anything you did below.

events.text: You lower a line into the cloud sea, out of boredom. Something bites. It is a fish made of mist, silver and nearly weightless, and it looks at you with great offence.

choices.text: Let it go at once

effects.log: It swims off into the white, flicking its tail at you. The next morning there are three of them under your island, curious.

choices.text: Study how it swims

effects.log: It swims by not quite existing. You try it with your own qi. For an afternoon you are slightly less there.

choices.text: Breathe in the mist it leaves behind

effects.log: Cold and sweet, like the air before snow. The fish sulks, but it has more mist where that came from.

events.text: On an empty isle a white jade stair climbs nine hundred steps and stops in the air. Whoever built it ascended, or gave up, or ran out of jade. The last step is worn smooth by someone who sat there a very long time.

choices.text: Climb to the top and sit where they sat

effects.log: The view is good. The wind is good. You understand, slowly, why someone stopped building.

choices.text: Read the carvings on the risers

effects.log: A builder's notes, nine hundred steps of them. The last one says only: enough. You copy it down for the court archive.

choices.text: Add one step of your own

effects.log: Cloud jade, cut by sword qi, set with care. Now the stairs go nowhere, plus one. It feels like a reply.

events.text: A grey monkey with gold eyes is up a tree in the Peach Garden, stuffing heavenly peaches into its cheeks. The gardeners are three isles away. The monkey sees you seeing it and freezes, mid-chew.
events.arc: The Monkey in the Peach Garden

choices.text: Catch it

ok.log: You catch it by the tail. It spits a peach stone at you with real accuracy. The gardeners send a thank-you. The monkey does not.

fail.log: It leads you up through every branch in the garden and leaves you hanging from the highest one. (-8 health)

choices.text: Pretend you saw nothing

effects.log: That evening a peach appears on your doorstep with one bite out of it. A bribe, or a friendship. Up here they are much alike.

choices.text: Ask it, politely, to share

effects.log: It considers you for a long time. Then it throws you a peach, hard. You catch it. You are, apparently, friends.

events.text: In a quiet garden there is a round pond that shows the world below instead of the sky. Right now it shows a market town you once walked through. It has grown. The old well is still in the square.

choices.text: Watch a whole day pass down there

effects.log: A cart, a quarrel, a wedding, rain. By evening you know three people's names. None of them will ever know yours.

choices.text: Drop a leaf on the water

effects.log: Down below, a child at the well looks up as a leaf falls from a clear sky. They keep it, you think. You hope.

choices.text: Look for the faces you knew

effects.log: They are gone. Their noses are not. You find the old tailor's nose on a young porter and laugh out loud.

events.text: Tonight is a festival in the world below. Sky lanterns come drifting up through the clouds, thousands of them, each one carrying somebody's wish. Most burn out. A few, against all reason, arrive.

choices.text: Catch one and read the wish

effects.log: A girl wants her brother home from the border. You cannot do much. You do what you can. Next year he is home.

choices.text: Breathe their light in

effects.log: Hope burns warm. It tastes of oil and rice paper. You feel younger than you have any right to.

choices.text: Light one of your own and send it down

effects.log: It sinks through the clouds, the wrong way. Somewhere a farmer will find a lantern from heaven and not know what to wish.

events.text: A heavenly deer has calved on your island in the night. The calf is white as new snow, its antlers are two buds of jade, and it has decided you are its mother. It follows you everywhere. It eats your sandals.

choices.text: Raise it until it can fly

effects.log: A season of following you around. Then one morning it leaps into the clouds and does not come down. It visits every spring.

choices.text: Find its real herd

ok.log: Seven isles away, a herd of white deer. The mother touches her nose to your forehead. You feel blessed, a little damp.

fail.log: You never find the herd. The herd finds you, much later, and takes the calf home without a word.

choices.text: Feed it from your own qi

effects.log: It drinks your qi like milk and grows a hand taller overnight. In its eyes you can see what you gave it.

events.text: On a bare isle two immortals stand mid-duel, swords raised, and have stood so long that moss has grown on their shoulders. They are not statues. Their eyes move. Each is waiting for the other to blink first.

choices.text: Clear your throat loudly

effects.log: Both blink. Both claim the other blinked first. The duel resumes after five thousand years, louder. You leave quickly.

choices.text: Study the frozen strike

effects.log: Two perfect strikes, each one the answer to the other. Nobody can win. You see now why nobody has moved.

choices.text: Brush the moss off their shoulders

effects.log: They do not thank you. They cannot. But the left one's eyes are wet, and the right one's are too.

events.text: An isle of hot springs, where the steam rises up into the sky instead of into the air. Three immortals are soaking up to their chins. They have been arguing about the same poem for six hundred years.

choices.text: Get in and pick a side

effects.log: You choose a fourth side, which nobody had thought of. For a hundred years they will call you the Fourth Bather.

choices.text: Get in and stay silent

effects.log: The water is very good. The argument is very bad. Both are restful in their way.

choices.text: Recite the poem correctly

ok.log: The silence after is the first in six hundred years. Then all three start arguing with you.

fail.log: You get the third line wrong. Now there are four versions. They thank you, bitterly.

events.text: A small star has fallen, but up here things fall the wrong way. It has rolled to a stop in a gully on your isle, humming, too hot to touch, about the size of a melon.

choices.text: Wait three days for it to cool

effects.log: It cools to black metal with light still moving inside it. You keep it under your bed. It hums you to sleep.

choices.text: Take its heat into your meridians

ok.log: It pours into you like boiling honey. For a year you glow faintly at night. The cranes avoid you.

fail.deathCause: burned from within by a fallen star
fail.log: The heat is too much. You throw up starlight for a week. (-30 health)

choices.text: Roll it back to the star river

effects.log: It takes all night. When you push it into the river it shoots up and takes its place. One star in the sky is brighter now.

events.text: A grand gate stands on a lawn in the Jade Court with no wall on either side. Courtiers walk the long way through it rather than around it. To walk around is, apparently, an insult to someone.

choices.text: Walk through, bowing like the rest

effects.log: A gatekeeper nods at you. You have been noticed doing nothing wrong, which at court is a kind of honour.

choices.text: Walk around it

effects.log: Silence across the lawn. Somebody faints. By evening you are famous among people who disapprove of you.

choices.text: Ask why it is there

effects.log: Nobody knows. An archivist finally finds the answer: a wall was planned. Eleven thousand years ago. It is still planned.

events.text: A letter is snagged in the pine on your island. It was sent upward by some mortal, burned at a grave, and the smoke carried it here. It is addressed to someone who died three hundred years ago.
events.arc: A Letter Caught in a Pine

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: A son tells his father the harvest was good and the roof is fixed. That is all. It is enough to make you sit down.

choices.text: Carry it on to the Hall of Departed Souls

effects.log: A clerk stamps it and files it. "Delivered," the clerk says. You choose to believe it.

choices.text: Write an answer and send it down

effects.log: You write as a father would, short and gruff: good harvest, good roof, good son. You hope it is not a crime.

events.text: The cranes of the Upper Realm carry letters between isles. Their roost is a crooked tower of nests, and the head crane has lost a letter for the first time in four thousand years. It is pacing.

choices.text: Search the cloud sea for it

ok.log: You find it on a cloud whale's back. The head crane bows so low it tips over. Your post is never late again.

fail.log: No letter. But you learn the cloud currents better than any immortal alive, which is a strange thing to be good at.

choices.text: Help sort the backlog meanwhile

effects.log: You read the addresses of a hundred immortals. You now know who writes to whom. You will never tell. Probably.

choices.text: Tell it that letters get lost

effects.log: The crane looks at you as if you have said the sky is optional. It goes back to pacing.

events.text: The star river crosses the night side of the Upper Realm, ankle deep and freezing. Each star you step on rings like a small bell. On the far bank someone has left a pair of sandals neatly, as if they will be back.

choices.text: Wade across slowly, listening

effects.log: The notes make a tune. It is not finished. You think it was started before the first immortal ascended.

choices.text: Scoop starwater into a jar

effects.log: It shines in the jar for a week. Then it is just very good water, the best you have tasted.

choices.text: Wait by the sandals for the owner

effects.log: Nobody comes in a month. You leave a note in one sandal. Ninety years later, a reply arrives.

events.text: The Western Pavilion holds its banquet, which happens every ten thousand years and lasts for one. You are seated between an immortal who only eats light and one who has not stopped talking since the soup.
events.arc: A Banquet of Ten Thousand Years

choices.text: Toast the host with a poem

ok.log: The hall is quiet, then loud. The host has it carved on a pillar. You will never be able to write anything that good again.

fail.log: Your poem rhymes "jade" with "jade". Someone coughs for three days. (-5 fame)

choices.text: Listen to the talker

effects.log: Inside a year of chatter are three secrets of the court and one recipe. You keep all four.

choices.text: Eat light with the quiet one

effects.log: It tastes of mornings. Neither of you says a word. At the end, the quiet one bows to you.

events.text: In the ruins of an immortal's palace an array still glows on the floor. Its maker is long gone. The array is still doing its work: patiently keeping a single flower alive in the middle of the rubble.

choices.text: Study the array

effects.log: Twelve thousand years of upkeep in a few thousand lines. Elegant. A little sentimental. You copy what you can.

choices.text: Feed qi into it

effects.log: The glow steadies. The flower lifts its head. You will come back. Somebody has to.

choices.text: Pick the flower

effects.log: The array goes dark the moment the stem breaks. It had nothing else to do. You feel it all the way home.

events.text: Two immortals sit at opposite ends of a long isle, back to back, each pretending the other is not there. Between them grows a pine. Their feud began over who planted it. That was seven thousand years ago.

choices.text: Ask each who planted it

effects.log: Both say they did. Both are lying. A bird planted it. You decide never to say so.

choices.text: Prune the pine for both of them

effects.log: They both watch furiously. When you are done, both agree it looks better. It is the first thing they have agreed on.

choices.text: Sit under it and say nothing

effects.log: Three immortals, one tree, no words. It is the most peaceful afternoon you have had in a century.

events.text: Your island floats above an old shrine in the world below. Today, through the clouds, you can hear someone praying. They pray to you, by your name. They have the name slightly wrong.

choices.text: Answer the prayer quietly

effects.log: A small rain, a good well, a sick goat that gets up. The shrine will be very busy next year.

choices.text: Listen without answering

effects.log: They ask for small things. A good husband for a daughter, a dry roof. Nobody below asks for the sky.

choices.text: Correct the name with a thunderclap

effects.log: They fall flat on their faces. The next day there is a new carving on the shrine. It is still slightly wrong.

events.text: In the Garden of Heavenly Beasts, a qilin grazes, a nine-coloured bird preens, and a very old tortoise is carrying a whole pavilion on its back. The keeper is asleep. A gate has blown open.

choices.text: Close the gate before anything leaves

effects.log: The keeper wakes up to find everything in place and you sitting on the wall. You are offered tea and a job. You take the tea.

choices.text: Ride the tortoise for a while

effects.log: It walks very slowly. You see the whole garden, and then you see it again, and you understand it is the point.

choices.text: Feed the nine-coloured bird

effects.log: It eats from your palm and drops a feather. When you get home your robe has changed colour. It stays changed.

events.text: Behind a waterfall that falls upward you find a vault, its seals faded to nothing. Inside are treasures sorted on shelves by someone very tidy. A label on the door says: back soon. The dust says otherwise.
events.arc: The Vault of the Forgotten Immortal

choices.text: Take one thing and leave a note

effects.log: You write your name and your isle. If the owner comes back, you will explain. You quite hope they do.

choices.text: Take nothing and reseal it

effects.log: Back soon might be true. Up here soon is a long word. You put a new seal on the door, a good one.

choices.text: Search for the owner instead

ok.log: You find them asleep on a cloud, for nine thousand years. They wake, thank you, and pay you in jade.

fail.log: No owner. But in the search you read their tidy notes on half the isles in the realm.

events.text: The great cloud whale is passing again, slow as a season. This time it swims low enough to touch. On its back is a little village of hermits who have lived up there for so long they have forgotten where it goes.

choices.text: Climb up and travel with them

effects.log: A year on the whale's back. You see the far side of the realm. It looks a lot like this side, but quieter.

choices.text: Bring them news of the court

effects.log: They want every scandal of the last thousand years. You run out after three days. They still thank you.

choices.text: Listen to the whale sing

effects.log: The song is so low you hear it with your bones. When it is over, your qi has been rearranged, neatly.

events.text: Immortals do not use money. They trade favours, and a whole isle is given over to it. Favours are written on jade slips and haggled over for centuries. A broker offers you a favour owed by the Eastern Pavilion.

choices.text: Trade one of your own favours for it

effects.log: You now own a favour from the Eastern Pavilion. You will never use it. Owning it is the point.

choices.text: Ask what favours cost here

effects.log: Two hours of explanation. You leave knowing who owes whom across the whole realm. It is like reading a map of grudges.

choices.text: Decline politely

effects.log: The broker looks at you with new respect. Nobody declines. You have done the one thing that makes you interesting.

events.text: A tribulation cloud has gathered over the next isle, purple and swollen. Under it a young immortal is trying to break through to the next realm and is clearly not ready. The lightning is already loading.

choices.text: Stand beside them and share the strikes

ok.log: Two of you take nine strikes meant for one. They break through. You have a friend for ten thousand years.

fail.deathCause: struck down by a tribulation not their own
fail.log: The heavens do not like a second guest. The fourth strike is just for you. (-32 health)

choices.text: Shout advice from a safe distance

effects.log: Half your advice is good. They use that half. They break through, smoking, and wave.

choices.text: Study the cloud while it works

effects.log: Tribulation clouds have a grammar. Yours was a sentence. This one is a question. You will need that one day.

events.text: A still lake on a high isle reflects a different face for each person who looks in. Yours shows someone who never left the village: a farmer, grey-haired, laughing in a doorway with a bowl of rice.
events.arc: The Lake of Your Other Lives

choices.text: Watch the farmer's life to its end

effects.log: A small, full life, eighty years. You are not jealous. You are a little jealous.

choices.text: Look away at once

effects.log: Some roads are better not walked twice. You go home and eat a bowl of rice in your doorway, just in case.

choices.text: Wave at the farmer

effects.log: After a moment, the farmer waves back. Then goes inside and shuts the door, which is fair.

events.text: A library drifts through the realm on its own isle, shelves open to the wind. It carries every scroll an immortal has ever written and lost. The librarian is a tortoise. It is not in a hurry to help you.

choices.text: Read until it drifts away again

effects.log: Three months of reading. You learn a little of everything and one thing very well. The tortoise allows it.

choices.text: Search for the scroll you lost

ok.log: It is there, filed under embarrassing. Your notes from the world below, in your young hand.

fail.log: You do not find it. The tortoise blinks at you. You feel strangely forgiven.

choices.text: Donate a scroll of your own

effects.log: You write down your fighting style. The tortoise files it, slowly, between two great masters.

events.text: A black cat lives in the Jade Court and belongs to nobody. It has sat in the empty Emperor's chair, and so, by an ancient rule nobody can disprove, it outranks everyone. It has chosen to sit on your lap.
events.arc: The Cat of the Jade Court

choices.text: Stay very still all afternoon

effects.log: Courtiers bow to the cat, which means they bow to your lap. By nightfall you are a minister in all but name.

choices.text: Ask it, gravely, for a ruling

effects.log: It licks its paw. The court records this as a yes. Nobody knows to what. Everyone assumes it was a yes to you.

choices.text: Get up anyway

effects.log: Gasps. The cat leaves. A scandal, briefly, until somebody else spills tea on it. (-3 fame)

events.text: Two old immortals play go with floating isles for stones. The board is half the sky. A game has run for nine centuries. One of them has fallen asleep and the other asks you to play for them.

choices.text: Play the sleeper's side

ok.log: You move one isle a single league. Nine centuries later, people still argue whether it was genius.

fail.log: Your move loses a corner of the sky. The sleeper wakes, looks, and goes back to sleep.

choices.text: Refuse, and wake the sleeper

effects.log: The sleeper wakes, makes the move you would have made, and winks. You go home oddly proud.

choices.text: Watch from the edge of the board

effects.log: The isles shifting past are like slow thoughts. Watching them is a meditation you did not know you needed.

events.text: Beyond the last mapped isle stands the palace of the first immortal, who ascended before there was a court. Its doors are open. Inside, everything is made for someone a little larger than anyone is now.
events.arc: The Palace of the First Immortal

choices.text: Sit on the great chair

effects.log: Your feet do not reach the floor. From here, the first immortal looked at an empty sky and decided to fill it.

choices.text: Read the wall carvings

effects.log: Not history. Instructions. Nobody could read them. Neither can you, quite, but you are closer.

choices.text: Bow at the threshold and leave

effects.log: The doors close slowly behind you. The palace was not abandoned, you think. It was waiting for someone to bow.

events.text: The isles end. Beyond is nothing, not even cloud. An old immortal is sitting on the very last rock with their feet over the edge, throwing pebbles into the nothing. They never hear them land.

choices.text: Sit beside them and throw one

effects.log: Your pebble falls for ever. So, you suspect, will theirs. Somehow that makes you both laugh.

choices.text: Look into the nothing for a long time

ok.log: It looks back. It is not hostile. It is only very patient. You come home seeing further than you did.

fail.deathCause: lost in the nothing beyond the edge of the Upper Realm
fail.log: The nothing pulls at your thoughts. It takes a year to remember your name. (-30 health)

choices.text: Ask why they come here

effects.log: "It is the only place up here nobody argues," they say. You come back next year. They have kept your rock.

events.text: A dragon's skeleton lies across three isles like a fallen bridge. Its bones are jade now. Pines grow from its eye sockets, and cranes nest in its ribs. It died, they say, of old age, which up here is very rare.
events.arc: The Bones of a Sky Dragon

choices.text: Walk its spine from tail to head

effects.log: A day's walk. Its qi is still in the bones, slow and warm. By the skull you feel a hundred years younger.

choices.text: Collect a fallen scale

effects.log: Green and cool, the size of your palm. It is still slightly warm in the middle.

choices.text: Light incense at the skull

effects.log: The cranes go quiet. Something in the bones settles. You think it had been waiting for a visitor.

events.text: High above the highest isle a door hangs in the air, old wood, iron rings. It is a little open. Through it comes a smell of rain on hot stone and someone very far away humming.

choices.text: Knock

effects.log: The humming stops. A pause. Then it starts again, a little closer. You decide that was an answer.

choices.text: Look through the gap

effects.log: Another sky, another sea of clouds, and an isle with a small figure on it looking back at you through another door.

choices.text: Close it gently

effects.log: It closes with a click. Somewhere the humming goes on. Some doors you leave for later. You have time.

events.text: Someone has to dust the empty Emperor's throne. The duty passes by lot. This year the lot fell on you. Behind you, both Pavilions watch to see whether you will touch the seat.

choices.text: Dust it perfectly and touch nothing more

effects.log: Both Pavilions are disappointed. That is the best result at court. You are trusted a little more.

choices.text: Sit in it for a heartbeat

ok.log: Nothing happens. Then the court decides something happened. You are a legend now, and suspected of everything.

fail.deathCause: struck down by the Jade Throne for sitting where no one may
fail.log: The throne disagrees. Lightning out of a clear hall. (-30 health)

choices.text: Dust the forgotten corners instead

effects.log: Under the throne you find a ten-thousand-year-old note: "Back in a moment." You put it back.

events.text: On this isle a vow of silence has held for twenty thousand years. The immortals who live here talk with their hands, their eyes and their tea. They have very strong opinions. You can tell.

choices.text: Stay a year and learn their hand speech

effects.log: By spring you can argue in it. By summer you have lost an argument in it, silently, and enjoyed it.

choices.text: Sneeze

effects.log: Twenty thousand years. Your sneeze echoes for a minute. They forgive you, with their eyes, at length.

choices.text: Meditate in the quiet

effects.log: No words means no wasted qi. You fill up like a pond after rain.

events.text: On a black isle lie the scorch marks of every immortal who failed a tribulation. Not graves: just the shapes they left in the rock, frozen at the moment of the last strike. Some are reaching up.

choices.text: Read the shapes and learn

effects.log: Each one made one mistake. You count the mistakes. You have made eleven of them yourself, and lived.

choices.text: Lay a pine branch on each

effects.log: It takes three days. There are more than you thought. The last one, a small shape, is holding hands with another.

choices.text: Call a little thunder to remember them

effects.log: A soft rumble, no strike. The rock stays quiet. You think, if they could, they would nod.

events.text: An immortal smith works a forge at the bottom of the star river, hammering stars flat into blades. The anvil is a moon. The smith wants an assistant who will not complain about the heat.

choices.text: Work the bellows for a season

effects.log: Hot, dark, deafening. At the end the smith hands you a sliver of star. You keep it in your sleeve. (-6 health)

choices.text: Ask to forge one blade yourself

ok.log: Your blade is crooked and burns with a cold light. The smith keeps it and gives you raw metal. A compliment, you think.

fail.log: The star splits and the smith sighs a very old sigh. You learn a great deal about failure. (-10 health)

choices.text: Watch and ask nothing

effects.log: The smith never speaks. You learn more about patience from one hammer than from a thousand masters.

events.text: On a mossy isle an immortal has been asleep for thirty thousand years. Flowers grow from their sleeves. The court sends someone every century to check they are still breathing. This century it is you.

choices.text: Check, write the report, leave

effects.log: Breathing. Snoring, slightly. You note it in the report. The clerk is delighted by the detail.

choices.text: Sit by them for a day

effects.log: Their breath is slow as tides. Your own falls in with it. You wake up next week, rested for a decade.

choices.text: Whisper the news of the last age

effects.log: You tell them who won what, and who married whom. Their mouth twitches. One of the flowers turns toward you.

events.text: From the highest isle the whole world below is the size of a plate. You can see the river you were born near, the mountain where you trained, and the long war that is happening this century, all at once.
events.arc: The World Below, From the Very Top

choices.text: Watch the war and grieve

effects.log: They fight over a pass you once crossed with a bag of rice. From up here it is very clear nobody will win.

choices.text: Cover the war with a cloud

effects.log: Three days of fog on the battlefield. Nobody can fight. Some generals go home. History calls it a miracle.

choices.text: Look only at your birthplace

effects.log: The river has moved. The village has not. A child is fishing exactly where you used to.

events.text: An immortal kept a pool of the faces of everyone they loved below, so as not to forget. The immortal is gone. The faces remain, drifting in the water, smiling at nobody.

choices.text: Learn their faces for them

effects.log: Two hundred faces. You learn them all. It seems only right that someone should.

choices.text: Add the faces you remember

effects.log: You add everyone you knew below. The water takes them. It is a relief, putting them down somewhere safe.

choices.text: Let them sink and rest

effects.log: One by one, they settle. The water turns clear. You think the owner would have wanted it eventually.

events.text: A sword stands upright in a cloud, as if the cloud were stone. Nobody has been able to pull it out in eight thousand years. The court has a long list of names of those who tried. Some of them were very famous.

choices.text: Try to pull it out

ok.log: It comes out easily, as if waiting. Then you put it back. The court cannot decide whether to honour you or panic.

fail.log: Your name goes on the list. You are in very good company, and you take some comfort in that.

choices.text: Ask the sword what it wants

effects.log: Nothing. It wants nothing. That is why nobody can pull it out. You walk home lighter.

choices.text: Leave a cup of wine beside it

effects.log: The next day the cup is empty. The court records it as wind. You know better.

events.text: A heavenly deer has been eating the herbs on your island all winter. It is the size of a horse, white with jade antlers, and completely unashamed. This morning it is back, with a friend.

choices.text: Share the herbs with them

effects.log: They eat everything but the weeds. In return, they keep the weeds down. A fair arrangement.

choices.text: Chase them off with a shout

effects.log: They leave, offended. You have a feeling they will be back with more friends.

events.text: The deer are back. All of them. Some hundred white deer stand on your island, quietly eating it. At their head is a stag so old its antlers have grown into a small tree, with birds nesting in them.

choices.text: Bow to the old stag

effects.log: It bows back. In the morning they are gone. Your herbs grow back twice as strong. The stag left a gift.

choices.text: Ride the stag across the realm

effects.log: It lets you, for a day. You see a hundred isles at the pace of a deer. The court is very jealous.

choices.text: Ask them, firmly, to leave

effects.log: They go, slowly, with dignity. The stag leaves you a single antler tip. It hums with qi.

events.text: It rains in the Upper Realm once a century, and the rain falls up. Today it rains. Immortals come out of their pavilions with their faces turned to the ground, laughing, catching drops on their chins.

choices.text: Go out and get soaked

effects.log: You come back wet from the feet up. You have not laughed like that since you were a child below.

choices.text: Collect the rain in jars

effects.log: Rain that falls up is very rare. You will drink one jar in a hundred years, to remember today.

choices.text: Watch from the doorway

effects.log: Ancient beings, giggling in the wet. Eternity has not made them any less silly. It is a comfort.

events.text: You wake up wanting noodles. Proper noodles from a stall below, with too much pepper. Nobody up here makes them. Immortals eat dew and light and peaches. The craving does not care.

choices.text: Try to make them yourself

ok.log: It takes eleven failed batches and a lot of cloud flour. They are almost right. Half the court wants the recipe.

fail.log: Your noodles float off the plate. Everything floats up here. You eat them out of the air, sadly.

choices.text: Sit with the craving until it passes

effects.log: It takes a long, hungry season. It passes. It is still there, underneath, and you are glad.

choices.text: Look down at a noodle stall all day

effects.log: You watch a cook pull noodles for eight hours. It is very satisfying. You are still hungry.

events.text: You notice dust on your pavilion's floor. It has been settling for longer than you have been counting. You did not notice because nothing up here is in a hurry. Neither, it turns out, were you.

choices.text: Sweep it all out, properly

effects.log: Under the dust, the floor is a beautiful green jade. You had forgotten. You decide to sweep once a decade.

choices.text: Read what the dust remembers

effects.log: A footprint from your first year here. Small, uncertain. You put a cloth over it and sweep around.

choices.text: Leave it: dust is honest

effects.log: Your neighbours think you are very wise or very lazy. Up here, nobody can tell the difference.

events.text: You realise today is your birthday. You only know because you counted. Nobody up here keeps birthdays. They have had too many. You are not sure how old you are going to be. Old.

choices.text: Throw yourself a quiet feast

effects.log: Peach, dew, a single cup of wine. A crane comes to watch. You let it have a bite. It is a good party.

choices.text: Go to the edge and look down

effects.log: Down below, a child is born somewhere about now. You wish them the long life you had, and a shorter one.

choices.text: Tell nobody and train all day

effects.log: Another year, another hundred thousand strikes. Your sword does not know it is your birthday. That is restful.

events.text: A rumour is going round the Jade Court, and the rumour is about you. You did a scandalous thing, apparently, with a cloud whale and an Eastern minister. You have no idea what. Nobody will tell you.

choices.text: Start a worse rumour about yourself

effects.log: Now you robbed the moon. Nobody remembers the whale. You are enjoying this more than you should.

choices.text: Track the rumour to its source

ok.log: It was the minister. He was bored. You come to an understanding. He sends you peaches every year.

fail.log: You question so many courtiers that a new rumour starts: that you are hunting someone. Now people avoid you.

choices.text: Ignore it for a hundred years

effects.log: It dies down by itself. Up here everything does, eventually. Including, you suppose, you.

events.text: Clearing a chest, you find the robe you wore when you climbed the white jade stairs. It is patched, travel-worn, faintly smelling of the world below: smoke, rice, rain on dust.

choices.text: Put it on for a day

effects.log: Immortals stare. Some smile. One old immortal touches the patch and says: "Mine was blue."

choices.text: Hang it on the wall

effects.log: Now every morning you see where you came from. Some mornings that is a comfort. Some mornings it is a joke.

choices.text: Burn it as an offering to the world below

effects.log: The smoke sinks through the clouds the wrong way. Somewhere below, a village smells rice and rain.

events.text: A crane lands on your isle, exhausted, carrying a letter sent from below. It was sent the year you ascended. It has been flying ever since. The ink has faded to nearly nothing.

choices.text: Read what is left

effects.log: Three words still visible: "proud of you." The rest you fill in yourself. You fill it in kindly.

choices.text: Nurse the crane back to strength

effects.log: It stays with you for a century. It is very bad-tempered. You would not part with it now.

choices.text: Write a reply to whoever sent it

effects.log: The writer is long dead. You write anyway. The crane takes it down, and does not come back. You hope it found someone.

events.text: You decide to plant a garden of heavenly pines. They grow one inch a century. If all goes well, in ten thousand years you will have shade. You have, you realise, the time.
events.arc: A Garden That Takes a Millennium

choices.text: Plant them in a careful pattern

effects.log: A pattern only visible from far above. You will see it in nine thousand years. It is something to look forward to.

choices.text: Plant them anyhow and see

effects.log: The pines grow where they like. In a thousand years it looks very natural, and the cranes approve.

choices.text: Invite the neighbours to plant one each

effects.log: Twenty immortals each plant one pine. It is the first time they have all been in one place without a feud.

events.text: In the middle of meditation you realise you have forgotten the name of your first teacher. The face, the voice, the smell of their tea, all there. The name is gone. It has been a long time.

choices.text: Search your memory until it comes

ok.log: Three days. Then it comes back, suddenly, like a bird landing. You write it on the pavilion wall.

fail.log: It does not come. You write their face in ink instead. The name, it turns out, was the least of them.

choices.text: Look down and find their grave

effects.log: It takes a year of looking. The name is carved there, worn but legible. You say it out loud, twice.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: Names are for the world below. Up here you have what mattered. You do not sleep well for a week.

events.text: Your isle has drifted above a farming village in the world below. Through the gap in the clouds you watch its people every day. This year their rice is failing. A drought sits on them like a stone.

choices.text: Send a small rain, secretly

effects.log: One soft night's rain. They do not know where it came from. The rice lifts its head.

choices.text: Watch and do nothing

effects.log: Up here they say: never meddle below. You keep the rule. You do not sleep.

events.text: Years later the village under your isle has built a little shrine. The carving on it is a cloud with a face. It is a terrible likeness. Children leave rice balls there, which float up to you, somehow, every autumn.

choices.text: Eat the rice balls, gratefully

effects.log: Cold, a bit squashed, perfect. You have eaten heavenly peaches. These are better.

choices.text: Send them a good harvest in return

effects.log: A golden year. The shrine gets a new roof. The carving stays terrible. You would not change it.

choices.text: Drift on, so they do not depend on you

effects.log: You let the isle go. The shrine stays. In a hundred years they will remember a kind cloud, and manage.

events.text: Two great immortals of the court have stopped speaking, again. One insulted the other's calligraphy nine thousand years ago. The court is splitting. Both, separately, ask you to carry a message.

choices.text: Carry both messages, word for word

effects.log: Both messages are insults. Very elegant ones. You deliver them with a straight face.

choices.text: Soften both messages a little

effects.log: "Your brush is a broken twig" becomes "your brush has character." They are both confused. Good.

events.text: The feud has come to a head. The two immortals will settle it the old way: a calligraphy duel before the whole court. They each want you as the judge. Whoever loses will sulk for a thousand years.

choices.text: Judge honestly

effects.log: The loser sulks. The winner gloats. The court is pleased. For a thousand years, the realm is peaceful and very annoying.

choices.text: Declare a draw

effects.log: Both are outraged. Then both agree you have no taste. United against you, they become friends again.

choices.text: Hang both scrolls side by side

effects.log: Together the two scrolls make a single poem. Neither of them meant it to. Nobody speaks for a while.

events.text: Meditating at dawn, you notice the cloud sea below has stopped moving. Not slowed. Stopped. It takes you a long moment to understand that it is you who have moved, very fast, without leaving your seat.

choices.text: Follow the feeling deeper

effects.log: For a heartbeat you are everywhere you have ever been. Then you are back, with your legs asleep.

choices.text: Hold it as long as you can

effects.log: You hold it for nine days. When you let go, the clouds rush past, catching up. Your qi is a full river.

choices.text: Let it go and laugh

effects.log: Too much, too early. You laugh at yourself. The clouds start moving again, a little offended.

events.text: At night the stars of the Upper Realm are near enough to hear. Most of them are humming. One of them, for the last three nights, has been humming the first training chant you ever learned, slightly off-key.

choices.text: Hum it back, in key

effects.log: The star corrects itself. The other stars join in. For one night the sky sings a beginner's chant.

choices.text: Practise the old forms to it

effects.log: Your first stances, under a star's humming. They feel new. You find a mistake you have made ever since.

choices.text: Ask who taught it the chant

effects.log: It hums the answer: another immortal from your world, long ago. You are not the first. It helps.

events.text: You dream of your tribulation: the first strike, the second, the ninth. In the dream you notice something you missed at the time. The lightning was not trying to kill you. It was trying to teach you.

choices.text: Relive it, stroke by stroke

effects.log: Every strike was a question. You failed half of them and survived anyway. You try the answers now.

choices.text: Wake and practise what it taught

effects.log: You call a little lightning into your palm. It stings. It also makes sense. (-5 health)

choices.text: Let the dream go

effects.log: Some lessons are only for the night they come. You sleep the rest of the night like a child below.

events.text: You look at your hands one morning. They have not held a sword since the white jade stairs. They have held tea, brushes, a cat, a crane's leg. They are still the hands of a fighter. They do not seem to mind either way.

choices.text: Take up the sword again for a year

effects.log: The sword feels heavy for one day, then like water. Your hands remember everything, and forgive you.

choices.text: Make a new form with empty hands

effects.log: A form for holding tea that also breaks stone. You are rather proud of it. Nobody will ever see it.

choices.text: Fold them and rest

effects.log: There is nothing to grasp. You have been grasping for a lifetime. Your hands thank you.

events.text: A wind is blowing across the Upper Realm. It began a hundred years ago at one end and has not yet reached the other. Today it reaches you. It carries the scent of every isle it has crossed.
events.arc: The Wind That Takes a Century

choices.text: Breathe it all in

effects.log: Pine, peach, a forge, a banquet, someone's sorrow, rain. A century of the realm, in one breath.

choices.text: Ride it to see where it goes

effects.log: You let it carry you for a season. It goes nowhere special. That, it turns out, is the lesson.

choices.text: Stand against it, unmoved

effects.log: A century of wind, and you do not bend. Then you bend a little, and the wind goes round you, politely.

events.text: In meditation the face of an enemy you fought below comes back. You killed them, or they nearly killed you; it was so long ago the two run together. You are the only one who remembers the fight now.
events.arc: The Face of an Old Enemy

choices.text: Forgive them, and yourself

effects.log: The face softens. So does something in your chest you did not know was tight.

choices.text: Replay the fight and win it properly

effects.log: Nine hundred times you replay it. On the last, you win cleanly. It changes nothing. Your qi is better for it.

choices.text: Burn incense for them

effects.log: Somebody should. Their family is long gone. You are what remains of their story, oddly.

events.text: An immortal told you a joke at court, long ago. You did not understand it. This morning, cleaning your teeth, you suddenly do. You laugh so hard you fall off your isle.
events.arc: The Joke That Took Ten Thousand Years

choices.text: Fly to the court and laugh at them

effects.log: The immortal has forgotten telling it. When you explain, they laugh too, ages late. Friendship sealed.

choices.text: Wonder what else you missed

effects.log: Everything, probably. Every silence was a lesson. You start listening to the court quite differently.

choices.text: Keep laughing as you fall

effects.log: You fall for three days, laughing. You land on a cloud whale. It does not think it is funny.

events.text: You ask the heavens a question, out loud, the way you did as a youth below. For the first time in your life, you are near enough that they could answer. They do not. The silence is very large.

choices.text: Ask again, louder

effects.log: Still nothing. But on the third try, a single crane flies past, very close. You take it as a maybe.

choices.text: Answer the question yourself

effects.log: You realise you already knew. You knew below. You climbed all this way to hear yourself say it.

choices.text: Sit in the silence until it feels kind

effects.log: It takes a decade. Then the silence is not empty any more. It is just quiet, the good kind.

events.text: In deep meditation you find that your inner world has grown. There is a small sky in your golden core now, a tiny sea of clouds, and on it a single isle, very much like yours. Someone on it is meditating.

choices.text: Go deeper, to the isle inside

ok.log: The figure inside opens their eyes. They are you. They nod. You wake up larger than you were.

fail.log: Worlds within worlds. You lose the way back for a year. Your body nearly forgets you. (-30 health)

choices.text: Tend the little sky carefully

effects.log: You smooth the tiny clouds, water the tiny pine. Your breath deepens for a century.

choices.text: Leave it be and come back out

effects.log: Some doors are for later. It will still be there. So, now, will you.

events.text: {npc}, an immortal who ascended a century before you, has decided you are a rival. Not in fighting. In tea. {He} arrives each year with a new leaf and a smug face, and waits to see what you serve back.

choices.text: Serve your best and say nothing

effects.log: {He} tastes it. {His} face does something complicated. "Next year," {he} says, and leaves.

choices.text: Serve plain water from the star river

effects.log: {He} sips. {He} sips again. {He} bows very low. You have won, with water. {He} will never forgive you.

choices.text: Admit defeat and learn from {him}

effects.log: {He} is so delighted {he} teaches you everything. {He} is, you realise, very lonely. So are you.

events.text: {npc}, a minister of the Eastern Pavilion, visits with three gifts and a smile. {He} wants you to vote with the East on a matter of court ceremony: which way the cranes should face during the spring rites.

choices.text: Agree, and take the gifts

effects.log: The cranes face east. The West sulks for a century. You get a nice stone and a very sincere letter.

choices.text: Refuse, politely

effects.log: {He} smiles harder. You have made an enemy who will be very kind to you for a thousand years.

choices.text: Ask the cranes which way they prefer

effects.log: The cranes face north, unanimously. {He} is speechless. The court talks of nothing else.

events.text: {npc}, a gardener of the Peach Garden, has come to complain. {His} prize tree has stopped fruiting. {He} is certain it is sulking. {He} wants someone new to talk to it, as it is tired of {him}.

choices.text: Talk to the tree, seriously

effects.log: You tell it about the world below. It listens. Next spring, one peach. {He} weeps.

choices.text: Check its roots for blight

ok.log: A tiny worm of shadow from the abyss. You draw it out. In autumn {he} gives you the first peach.

fail.log: Nothing wrong with the roots. You both stare at the tree. The tree stares back.

choices.text: Tell {him} to rest, not the tree

effects.log: {He} takes a year off for the first time in eight thousand. The tree fruits immediately. Neither of you comments.

events.text: {npc} has just climbed the white jade stairs. {He} is from another world entirely, and {he} is lost, proud and trying very hard not to show either. {He} asks you, stiffly, where one might find somewhere to sit.

choices.text: Show {him} round the isles

effects.log: A month of tours. {He} asks good questions. By the end {he} is less proud, less lost, and a friend.

choices.text: Knock {him} off an isle, then help

effects.log: Someone did it for you once. {He} climbs back, furious, then laughs. "Everyone up here was the strongest," you say.

choices.text: Give {him} your spare cushion

effects.log: {He} sits. {He} cries a little. You look the other way. That is how you were welcomed too.

events.text: {npc}, a singer of the court, is writing a ballad about you. {He} has questions. {He} has already decided the answers. In {his} ballad you are seven feet tall and ascended on the back of a phoenix.
events.arc: The Immortal Who Sings Your Story

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth, every step

effects.log: {He} listens with growing disappointment. The ballad keeps the phoenix. "Art," {he} says.

choices.text: Add a dragon to the ballad

effects.log: Now there is a dragon and a phoenix. The court loves it. You hum it in the bath, privately.

choices.text: Ask {him} to sing it for you

effects.log: It is ridiculous and lovely. You hear your own life made enormous. It is good to hear, once.

events.text: {npc}, once a high minister, was exiled from the Jade Court for three thousand years for a reason nobody will say. {He} lives alone on a small isle, and has started rowing a cloud boat over to visit you.

choices.text: Ask why {he} was exiled

effects.log: {He} spilled tea on the empty Emperor's chair. That was all. {He} laughs. You both laugh.

choices.text: Speak for {him} at court

ok.log: The court remembers the tea, and laughs. The exile is lifted. {He} sends you one cloud plum a year, for ever.

fail.log: The court looks at you as if you had spilled tea yourself. {He} pats your arm. "Thank you for trying."

choices.text: Just keep {him} company

effects.log: Tea, go, silence. {He} is excellent company. Exile, you think, is only loneliness with a stamp on it.

events.text: {npc} has been counting the stars of the Upper Realm for twelve thousand years. {He} has lost count again. {He} asks, with great dignity, if you would hold this end of the string.

choices.text: Hold the string and count with {him}

effects.log: A century of counting. You reach the same number {he} reached last time. {He} is thrilled. It is still wrong.

choices.text: Tell {him} the number does not matter

effects.log: {He} looks at you with pity. "Everything up here does not matter," {he} says. "That is why we count."

choices.text: Bring {him} a fallen star for the total

effects.log: {He} counts it twice, by accident. You do not mention it. Some friendships run on small mercies.

events.text: {npc}, a young immortal of only four hundred, has decided you are a great master. {He} sits outside your pavilion every morning and will not leave until you teach {him} something.
events.arc: Someone Wants to Learn From You

choices.text: Teach {him} your first stance

effects.log: {He} practises it for a decade, very seriously. One day it is better than yours. You are prouder than you expected.

choices.text: Send {him} to sweep your floor

effects.log: {He} sweeps furiously for a year. Then, slowly, calmly. That was the lesson. {He} understands, finally.

choices.text: Admit you are still learning too

effects.log: {He} is astonished. Then {he} brings two cushions. You learn together. It is the best year in a century.
